A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a 3D fully-convolutional network for pancreas segmentation, that is able to process a 3-D image and produce an automatic volumetric pancreas segment in a single pass.

we have shown that a custom build 3D FCNs can be successfully applied to segmenting organs in medical imaging, and that it is possible to train a network on a relatively small dataset (N=147) and still achieve state-of-the-art results on a challenging task.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a 3D FCNs with a summation skip connections is able to achieve state-of-the-art results on a challenging pancreas dataset, and that the method is robust to different training data distributions and can be applied to new unseen patients.
a single 3D FCU can be trained to segment the entire pancreas from CT scans, without the need of a pre-segmentation step or a multi-step segmentation process, and with a high performance.
